items.title: Core Principles & the Evolution of Indian Foreign Policy
items.body:
India's foreign policy rests on a few enduring ideas that have adapted with time.

- **Panchsheel (1954)** — the *Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence*, first set out in the India-China agreement on Tibet (Nehru-Zhou Enlai): mutual respect for sovereignty & territorial integrity, mutual non-aggression, non-interference, equality & mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence.
- **Non-Alignment (NAM)** — refusal to join either Cold-War bloc; first summit at **Belgrade, 1961** (founders Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno, Nkrumah). It meant independence of judgement, not passivity.
- **Strategic autonomy / multi-alignment** — the modern successor to non-alignment: keep independent decision-making while partnering with many powers issue-by-issue.

**Phases:** Nehruvian idealism & non-alignment (1947-64) → realism after the 1962 war and 1971 Indo-Soviet Treaty → post-1991 economic diplomacy → post-2014 multi-alignment (Quad + BRICS/SCO simultaneously).

**Determinants:** geography (long coastline, Himalayan frontiers), history & anti-colonial values, economic needs (energy, markets), national capability (military/nuclear), domestic politics, and the international system. Foreign affairs is a Union executive function (Union List entries 10-14).
keyPoints: Panchsheel = Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, from the 1954 India-China Tibet agreement.
NAM's first summit was at Belgrade in 1961; founders included Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno, Nkrumah.
Strategic autonomy = independent decision-making while engaging multiple powers (multi-alignment).
Evolution: Nehruvian idealism -> post-1962/1971 realism -> post-1991 economic diplomacy -> post-2014 multi-alignment.
Determinants: geography, history/values, economic needs, national capability, domestic politics, international system.
items.source: MEA (Ministry of External Affairs), Government of India

items.title: Neighbourhood First, Gujral Doctrine, Act East & SAGAR
items.body:
India frames its regional engagement through named policies:

| Policy / Vision | Year | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| **Gujral Doctrine** | 1996 | *Non-reciprocity* — unilateral concessions to smaller neighbours (not Pakistan) to build trust |
| **Neighbourhood First** | 2014 | Priority to immediate South Asian neighbours; connectivity, aid, 'first responder' role |
| **Act East** | 2014 (from *Look East*, 1991) | ASEAN, East Asia & the Indo-Pacific — Culture, Commerce, Connectivity, Capacity |
| **SAGAR** | 2015 | 'Security And Growth for All in the Region' — maritime vision for the **Indian Ocean** |

**Neighbours snapshot (current):** *Bhutan* — closest partner, hydropower ties; *Nepal* — 1950 Treaty, open border, periodic friction over boundary maps; *Bangladesh* — ties strained after the August 2024 change of government (interim administration under Muhammad Yunus); *Sri Lanka* — economic-recovery support after the 2022 crisis; *Maldives* — recalibration after an initial 'India Out' phase; *Myanmar* — engagement despite post-coup instability; *Pakistan* — near-frozen ties, worsened by the 2025 Pahalgam attack.

India positions itself as a **'net security provider'** and 'first responder' (Vaccine Maitri, HADR missions) in the Indian Ocean Region.
keyPoints: Gujral Doctrine (1996) = non-reciprocity toward smaller neighbours (excludes Pakistan).
Neighbourhood First (2014) prioritises immediate South Asian neighbours.
Act East (2014) grew from Look East (1991); reaches ASEAN and the Indo-Pacific.
SAGAR (2015) = 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' — Indian Ocean maritime vision.
Bangladesh ties strained after Aug 2024 government change (interim govt under Muhammad Yunus).
India brands itself a 'net security provider' and 'first responder' in the IOR.
items.source: MEA (Ministry of External Affairs), Government of India; neighbour developments verified Sep 2026

items.title: Relations with Major Powers — US, Russia, China, Pakistan
items.body:
**India-US:** a 'Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership'. Foundational defence agreements — **LEMOA, COMCASA, BECA**; technology cooperation via **iCET (Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology, 2023)**; partners in the Quad.

**India-Russia:** a **'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'** rooted in the 1971 treaty legacy — defence (S-400, BrahMos, licensed production), nuclear energy (Kudankulam) and, since 2022, large discounted crude imports. India retained strategic autonomy on Ukraine, urging dialogue rather than condemnation.

**India-China:** cooperation (trade, BRICS, SCO) alongside rivalry along the un-demarcated **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**. The **Galwan clash (June 2020)** was the first fatal border incident since 1975; an **October 2024 patrolling agreement** for eastern Ladakh (Depsang, Demchok) enabled a Modi-Xi meeting at the Kazan BRICS summit.

**India-Pakistan:** dominated by **cross-border terrorism** and Kashmir. After the **Pahalgam attack (April 2025)**, India launched **Operation Sindoor (May 2025)** and held the **Indus Waters Treaty (1960) in abeyance**. Ties remain near-frozen; India insists 'talks and terror cannot go together'.
keyPoints: India-US foundational pacts: LEMOA, COMCASA, BECA; tech via iCET (2023).
India-Russia = 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'; S-400, BrahMos, Kudankulam, discounted oil.
LAC is undemarcated; Galwan clash was June 2020 (first fatal since 1975).
Oct 2024 India-China patrolling pact (Depsang, Demchok) preceded a Modi-Xi meeting at Kazan.
Operation Sindoor (May 2025) followed the Pahalgam attack (April 2025); Indus Waters Treaty held in abeyance.
items.source: MEA (Ministry of External Affairs), Government of India; developments verified Sep 2026

items.title: Key Groupings — Quad, BRICS, SCO, G20
items.body:
India practises **multi-alignment**, sitting in Western-leaning and Eurasian groupings at once.

| Grouping | Members / status | India's role |
|---|---|---|
| **Quad** | India, US, Japan, Australia | Diplomatic forum (not a military alliance); free & open Indo-Pacific; revived 2017, leaders' summits from 2021 |
| **BRICS** | 10 members (2025): Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa + Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Indonesia | NDB & Contingent Reserve Arrangement; India hosts the 2026 summit |
| **SCO** | China, Russia, Central Asian states, India, Pakistan, Iran | India a **full member since 2017**; counter-terror via RATS; chaired 2023 |
| **G20** | 19 countries + EU + **African Union** | India's **2023 presidency** admitted the AU as a permanent member ('Voice of the Global South') |

**Also:** I2U2 (India, Israel, UAE, US), BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal), IBSA, and India-led SAARC (largely dormant) vs. its preference for BIMSTEC. India champions the **Global South** and reform of global governance.
keyPoints: Quad (India, US, Japan, Australia) is a strategic dialogue, not a treaty alliance; revived 2017.
BRICS has 10 members from 2025 (added Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Indonesia); India hosts the 2026 summit.
India joined the SCO as a full member in 2017; SCO's counter-terror arm is RATS.
G20 = 19 countries + EU + African Union (AU added at India's 2023 New Delhi presidency).
India also engages via I2U2, BIMSTEC and IBSA, and champions the Global South.
items.source: MEA / G20 India Secretariat; BRICS communiqués; membership verified Sep 2026

items.title: UNSC Reform, Nuclear Doctrine & Global Governance
items.body:
**UNSC reform:** India seeks a **permanent seat** on an expanded UN Security Council through the **G4 (India, Japan, Germany, Brazil)**, whose members back one another's bids. The **'Uniting for Consensus' / Coffee Club** (Italy, Pakistan and others) opposes new permanent seats. India has served several terms as a non-permanent member and argues the Council is unrepresentative of 21st-century realities.

**Nuclear doctrine:** After **Pokhran-II (1998)**, India adopted (2003) a doctrine of **credible minimum deterrence**, **No First Use (NFU)**, and **massive retaliation** if attacked with WMD, plus a voluntary testing moratorium and civilian control (Nuclear Command Authority). The 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal and the NSG waiver eased India's nuclear isolation; India is a member of **MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement and the Australia Group**, but not the NSG or NPT.

**Soft power & diaspora:** the world's **largest diaspora** and top recipient of remittances; instruments include yoga (International Day of Yoga), Buddhism, cinema, and development partnership (lines of credit, ITEC training).
keyPoints: G4 = India, Japan, Germany, Brazil — seek permanent UNSC seats; opposed by 'Uniting for Consensus'.
Nuclear doctrine (2003): credible minimum deterrence, No First Use, massive retaliation, testing moratorium.
Pokhran-II tests were in 1998; the 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal + NSG waiver ended nuclear isolation.
India is in MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement and Australia Group; not in the NSG or NPT.
India has the world's largest diaspora and is the top recipient of remittances (soft power asset).
items.source: MEA (Ministry of External Affairs), Government of India

items.title: PYQ Precision — Memberships, Regimes, Geography & Corridors
items.body:
## India's grouping memberships (member vs not)

- **Member**: East Asia Summit (2005), SCO (2017), BRICS, G20, BIMSTEC, IORA, Quad, I2U2.
- **NOT a member**: **APEC**; ASEAN (only a **dialogue partner**); **AUKUS**; **NSG**; **RCEP** (withdrew 2019); NPT.
- **RCEP** = ASEAN + China, Japan, S.Korea, Australia, NZ; India withdrew in 2019.

## Export-control regimes

| Regime | India joined |
|---|---|
| MTCR | 2016 |
| Wassenaar Arrangement | 2017 |
| Australia Group | 2018 |
| **NSG** | **Not a member** (China blocks; NPT issue) |

## Strategic geography (news traps)

- **Golan Heights** = Israel-Syria; **Two-State Solution** = Israel-Palestine; **Siachen** (Saltoro Ridge) = India-Pakistan (Operation Meghdoot, 1984); **LAC** = India-China.

## Connectivity corridors

- **IMEC** (India-Middle East-Europe) announced at **G20 New Delhi 2023**; **INSTC** links India-Iran-Russia via **Chabahar**. India opposes China's **BRI/CPEC** (crosses PoK).
keyPoints: India is in the East Asia Summit but NOT in APEC and not an ASEAN member (only dialogue partner).
India withdrew from RCEP (2019); RCEP = ASEAN + China/Japan/S.Korea/Australia/NZ.
India joined MTCR (2016), Wassenaar (2017), Australia Group (2018) but NOT the NSG.
Golan = Israel-Syria; Two-State = Israel-Palestine; Siachen = India-Pakistan; LAC = India-China.
IMEC was announced at G20 New Delhi 2023; INSTC links India to Russia via Iran (Chabahar).
